defect_found_in_live_verification.what: The History view's provenance -- when each saved configuration was put in use, by whom and for what recorded reason -- was entirely dead. Every version rendered 'How this version came to be saved was not recorded'.
defect_found_in_live_verification.cause: The provenance query joined public.operators.id (uuid) to public.audit_log.actor_id (text). PostgreSQL has no uuid = text operator and refused the whole statement.
defect_found_in_live_verification.why_it_was_silent: That query's error is discarded on purpose, so losing the audit log can never cost an operator the configuration itself. The endpoint therefore answered 200 with empty provenance, which is indistinguishable from the legitimate no-audit-log case. Nothing was down and nothing complained.
defect_found_in_live_verification.why_no_test_caught_it: The disposable fixture builds public.audit_log with a created_at column, while the appliance's own 0001 migration names it ts. On the fixture the query fails for that second, unrelated reason, so asserting empty provenance there would have asserted the bug.
defect_found_in_live_verification.scope_of_harm: Presentation only. No guest state, stay state, PMS configuration, permission, audit record or reconciliation behaviour was affected -- the configuration itself always read from the configuration tables and was always correct.

correction.change: The join compares op.id::text to the recorded actor. Widening uuid to text always succeeds; casting the other way (actor_id::uuid) would parse every actor string in the audit log and throw on the first that is not a uuid -- and actor_id is text precisely because appliance-originated actions are recorded under names, not ids.
correction.single_source_of_truth: The statement is now the named constant pmsRevisionProvenanceSQL, executed verbatim by its regression test. There is no second copy to drift.
correction.regression_test: TestPmsRevisionProvenanceSQLRunsAgainstProductionColumnTypes builds audit_log and operators with PRODUCTION column types in a schema of its own and runs the real statement against them. It asserts the query executes, that a known operator is named, that a non-uuid unknown actor still appears with its reason intact and is given no invented name, and that the recorded actor identity survives verbatim.
correction.proven_to_fail_pre_fix: Reverting the cast makes it fail with 'operator does not exist: uuid = text (SQLSTATE 42883)'. A regression test that cannot fail proves nothing, so this was demonstrated rather than assumed.
correction.no_migration: None. No schema change; the column types were already correct and the query was wrong about them.
